task: Draft a 100–140-word methods clarification for an undergraduate program-evaluation assignment. Readers understand a mean and random assignment but are new to this workshop's participant flow. Explain why the reported mean cannot estimate the effect of being offered the workshop, and identify which outcome coverage is missing. Do not invent results for nonattendees or a causal effect size. The task is to explain the mismatch between the requested comparison and the available observations, not to design a new study or supply significance tests.

facts.text: Forty participants were randomly assigned: 20 were offered the fictional workshop and 20 were not.
Twelve of the 20 offered participants attended; eight did not.
Only ten attendees returned an outcome form; their mean end-of-exercise score was 6 on a 0–10 scale.
The packet gives no outcomes for the other two attendees, the eight offered nonattendees, or the 20 not offered the workshop.
The assignment asks about the effect of an offer, which concerns the originally assigned groups, not only attendees who returned forms.

forbidden_additions: A six-point treatment effect or any invented comparison-group mean
An assertion that random assignment eliminates missing-outcome or attendance-selection problems
Invented significance, confidence intervals, or completed follow-up
preserve: 40 assigned, 20 offered, 12 attended, ten attendee forms
The observed mean is an end score, not a change or effect estimate
Offer, attendance, and response are different stages
